questions.prompt: An App Service app needs more memory per worker and a higher-tier feature. Which operation addresses these requirements?

options.text: Scale up the App Service plan to a suitable SKU.
options.explanation: Scale up changes worker resources and tier features.

options.text: Only increase worker count with the existing SKU.
options.explanation: Scale out adds workers but does not increase memory per worker or unlock higher-tier features.
A slot consumes the existing plan capacity.

options.text: Only set a larger maximum autoscale count.
options.explanation: A count limit does not change the worker SKU.

questions.prompt: An App Service plan must run more instances at 08:00 each weekday based on a schedule. Which scaling mechanism should be used?

options.text: Azure Monitor autoscale with a scheduled profile.
options.explanation: Autoscale supports schedules for plan capacity.

options.text: App Service automatic scaling based only on HTTP traffic.
options.explanation: HTTP automatic scaling does not express the requested time-based schedule.
Swapping code slots does not define scheduled worker capacity.

options.text: A higher SKU without any scheduled scaling configuration.
options.explanation: Changing tier does not implement the requested daily instance schedule.

questions.prompt: You evaluate App Service automatic HTTP scaling. Which TWO points belong in the cost and compatibility review?

options.explanation: Automatic scaling reserves a buffer whose instance time is charged.

options.text: Deployment-slot traffic is unsupported for this scaling feature.
options.explanation: The documented automatic scaling feature does not scale based on slot traffic.

options.text: It is the same configuration as Azure Monitor schedule rules.
options.explanation: Automatic HTTP scaling and Azure Monitor autoscale are distinct.

options.text: It provides paid Premium features on Free plans.
options.explanation: The feature requires supported Premium tiers.
